title: Map OpenAI Responses feature semantics to Redwood runtime: lossiness taxonomy and tactical mitigations
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Background: Our hosted API must provide behavioral compatibility with the OpenAI Responses API for customers that depend on streaming events, function/tool calling semantics, and structured output envelopes. Existing parity work has focused on API surface and surface-level mapping; this ticket scopes a semantic mapping + lossiness taxonomy and proposes tactical runtime mitigations that keep apps stable during migration.
acceptance_criteria: Deliver a documented lossiness taxonomy that enumerates semantic gaps between OpenAI Responses and Redwood runtime for streaming, function calling, and structured outputs.
Produce a prioritized list of tactical mitigations with estimated implementation cost and measurable success criteria.
Implement a lightweight runtime shim prototype that demonstrates: event ordering preservation for streaming, deterministic tool_call signaling, and schema-tag passthrough for structured outputs.
Ship contract tests and a compatibility test harness that can run against OpenAI-like fixtures and real model outputs.
Publish a rollout plan (canary percentages, feature flags, fallback routes) and associated dashboards for monitoring regressions in output fidelity and latency overhead.
comments: 2025-01-10 - Asha K: Kickoff - collected gaps from support tickets and internal parity audits. Initial areas: (1) streaming chunking and event framing differences, (2) tool_call lifecycle (invocation vs streaming annotation), (3) structured output schema markers lost in our serializer.

2025-01-15 - Miguel O: Implemented first-pass inventory of behavioral deltas using model replay corpus (100k requests). Added preliminary lossiness categories: Header/metadata loss, Event fragmentation, Tool call transform, Schema flattening.

2025-01-22 - Meeting notes: Decided to prototype a ‘semantic envelope’ shim that attaches opaque metadata to streaming frames to preserve order and tool_call intent. Trade-offs: small token overhead vs fewer client-side patches.
2025-01-28 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8987 - runtime: add semantic envelope and event-id propagation. Prototype behind feature flag 'resp-compat-envelope'.

2025-01-31 - QA: Contract tests added for 4 streaming scenarios, 6 function-call variants, and 3 structured JSON-LD schemas. Found two edge cases: concurrent tool_call candidate selection and mid-stream schema patching (model edits schema after partial emit).

2025-02-02 - Miguel O: Updated mitigation list and moved ticket to In Progress. Next: implement deterministic ordering guarantees and add telemetry for lossiness signals (schema-mismatch rate, tool_call rejections).
test_plan: Create a model-replay suite covering streaming with partial JSON chunks, function_call proposals, and post-hoc structured-output patches.
Run contract tests against an OpenAI Responses fixture harness (synthetic event stream generator) and against a small set of live models in canary region.
Add unit tests for event-id propagation, ordering under induced packet loss, and serializer round-trip preservation.
Introduce Canary smoke checks that validate structured output schemas remain unchanged for a sampled set of requests.
Measure latency overhead introduced by shim (target < 5ms p50).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge prototype behind feature flag 'resp-compat-envelope' to staging (no customer traffic).
Phase 1: Internal dogfood with Redwood Console flows and SDK integration tests.
Phase 2: 1% production traffic in US region for 48 hours; monitor schema-mismatch-rate and function_call-failure-rate.
Phase 3: Increase to 10% for 72 hours; run end-to-end regressions and customer-facing smoke tests.
Phase 4: 50% with auto-rollback on signal thresholds; full rollout when metrics stable for 7 days.
Fallback: Automatic reroute to baseline runtime variant if token overhead > 3% or on detected semantic regressions.
notes: Measurement plan: add metrics 'resp.compat.lossy_event_rate', 'resp.compat.toolcall_reject_rate', and 'resp.compat.schema_delta_rate' to Console dashboards.
Operational alert thresholds to propose: lossiness rate > 0.5% sustained for 1 hour OR tool_call_reject_rate > 0.1%.
Longer-term: consider model-adaptive shims (per-model profiles) if we see large variance across model families.
Customer communication: draft migration notes for early adopters explaining token overhead and compatibility guarantees.
